title: Introduction to Vue Testing
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Introduction to Vue Testing in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Introduction to Vue Testing within Testing and Quality Assurance. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Testing behavior before release catches regressions in props, events, forms, asynchronous states, and routing.

content_blocks.title: Introduction to Vue Testing: Behavior-focused testing
content_blocks.alt_text: Behavior-focused testing diagram for lesson 115: Introduction to Vue Testing. Create known state and deterministic inputs → Trigger the user behavior or failure case → Check visible output, events, and errors
content_blocks.caption: Testing workflow: arrange a repeatable state, act as a user, then assert observable behavior including a boundary case.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Automated checks combine unit, component, interaction, integration, and end-to-end tests with repeatable quality gates. This lesson focuses on Introduction to Vue Testing. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Why automated testing matters
items.text: For Why automated testing matters, define the behavior a user can observe before writing the assertion. Test a typical case and one boundary/failure case, keep dependencies deterministic, and use component or browser tests only when that level adds confidence.

content_blocks.expected_output: Vitest reports the test as passing when a click emits increment. The test checks observable behavior rather than internal implementation details.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Install vitest, @vue/test-utils, and the Vue Vite plugin according to the current official testing guide; run npm test or the configured test script.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Introduction to Vue Testing with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Types of tests”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Automated checks combine unit, component, interaction, integration, and end-to-end tests with repeatable quality gates. For Introduction to Vue Testing, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Introduction to Vue Testing” that applies “Why automated testing matters”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Why automated testing matters”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Introduction to Vue Testing belongs to the broader area Testing and Quality Assurance.
The main concept to practice is Why automated testing matters.
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
